In [[abelian group|abelian]] [[group theory]], an abelian group is said to be '''cotorsion''' if any [[Group extension|extension]] of it by a [[torsion-free abelian group]] splits. If the group is <math>M</math>, this says that the [[Ext functor|Ext-group]] <math>\operatorname{Ext}_\mathbb{Z}(F,M)</math> is zero for all torsion-free groups <math>F</math>. Since any such <math>F</math> embeds into a direct sum of copies of <math>\mathbb{Q}</math>, it suffices to check the condition on the group of [[Rational number|rational numbers]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite book |last=Fuchs |first=László |url=https://link.springer.com/10.1007/978-3-319-19422-6 |title=Abelian Groups |date=2015 |publisher=Springer International Publishing |isbn=978-3-319-19421-9 |series=Springer Monographs in Mathematics |location=Cham |language=en |chapter=Chapter 9.6 |doi=10.1007/978-3-319-19422-6}}</ref>

Every [[divisible group]] or [[injective group]] (in particular the group of rational numbers <math>\mathbb{Q}</math>) is cotorsion. For any two abelian groups <math>A</math> and <math>B</math>, the group of extensions <math>\operatorname{Ext}_\mathbb{Z}(A,B)</math> is cotorsion.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Fuchs |first=László |url=https://link.springer.com/10.1007/978-3-319-19422-6 |title=Abelian Groups |date=2015 |publisher=Springer International Publishing |isbn=978-3-319-19421-9 |series=Springer Monographs in Mathematics |location=Cham |page=284 |language=en |chapter=Theorem 6.5 |doi=10.1007/978-3-319-19422-6}}</ref>

== Properties of cotorsion groups ==
The class of cotorsion groups is [[closed under]] extensions, [[Direct product of groups|direct products]], and [[Quotient group|quotients]].<ref name=":0" />

A [[Countable set|countable]] cotorsion group is a direct sum of a divisible group and a bounded group, that is a group of bounded [[Exponent of a group|exponent]].<ref name=":0" />

The '''Baer--Fomin Theorem''' states that a torsion group is cotorsion if and only if it is a [[Direct sum of groups|direct sum]] of a divisible group and a bounded group.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Baer |first=Reinhold |author-link=Reinhold Baer |date=1936 |title=The Subgroup of the Elements of Finite Order of an Abelian Group |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/1968617 |journal=Annals of Mathematics |volume=37 |issue=4 |pages=766–781 |doi=10.2307/1968617 |jstor=1968617 |issn=0003-486X|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Fomin |first=Sergei |author-link=Sergei Fomin |date=1937 |title=Über periodische Untergruppen der unendlichen Abelschen Gruppen |url=https://duckduckgo.com/?q=S.V.+Fomin%2C+Uber+periodische+Untergruppen+der+unendlichen+abelschen+Gruppen%2C+Mat.+Sb.+2+(1937)%2C+1007–1009.&t=osx&ia=web |journal=Matematicheskii Sbornik |volume=2 |issue=44 |pages=1007–1009}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Griffith |first=Phillip |date=2003-03-01 |title=The Baer splitting problem in the twentyfirst century |url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/illinois-journal-of-mathematics/volume-47/issue-1-2/The-Baer-splitting-problem-in-the-twentyfirst-century/10.1215/ijm/1258488150.full |journal=Illinois Journal of Mathematics |volume=47 |issue=1–2 |page=1 |doi=10.1215/ijm/1258488150 |issn=0019-2082}}</ref>

A torsion-free abelian group is cotorsion if and only if it is [[algebraically compact group|algebraically compact]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last=Van Leeuwen |first=L. C. A |date=1969-01-01 |title=On torsion-free cotorsion groups |url=https://dx.doi.org/10.1016/1385-7258%2869%2990041-9 |journal=Indagationes Mathematicae (Proceedings) |volume=72 |issue=4 |pages=388–393 |doi=10.1016/1385-7258(69)90041-9 |issn=1385-7258|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Fuchs |first=L. |date=1963-03-01 |title=Notes on abelian groups. II |url=https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02020629 |journal=Acta Mathematica Academiae Scientiarum Hungaricae |language=en |volume=11 |issue=1 |pages=117–125 |doi=10.1007/BF02020629 |issn=1588-2632|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Such groups are precisely the [[Direct summand|direct summands]] of direct products of [[P-adic number|<math>p</math>-adic integers.]]<ref name=":1" />

[[Ulm subgroup]]s of cotorsion groups are cotorsion and [[Ulm factor]]s of cotorsion groups are algebraically compact.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Fuchs |first=László |date=1959 |title=Notes on abelian groups. I. |journal=Annales Universitatis Scientiarum Budapestinensis |volume=2 |pages=5–23}}</ref>

== In ring theory ==
A [[Module (mathematics)|right module]] ''M'' over a [[Ring (mathematics)|ring]] ''R'' is said to be a '''cotorsion module''' if <math>\operatorname{Ext}^1_R(F,M)=0</math> for all [[Flat module|flat (right) modules]] ''F''.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Mao |first1=Lixin |last2=Ding |first2=Nanqing |date=October 2006 |title=Cotorsion modules and relative pure-injectivity |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/product/identifier/S1446788700015858/type/journal_article |journal=Journal of the Australian Mathematical Society |language=en |volume=81 |issue=2 |pages=225–244 |doi=10.1017/S1446788700015858 |issn=1446-7887}}</ref> When <math>R</math> is the ring of [[Integer|integers]] <math>\mathbb{Z}</math>, this reduces to the previous definition of cotorsion abelian groups. 

The ring <math>R</math> is said to be (right) cotorsion if the [[Regular representation|regular module]] <math>R_R</math> is cotorsion. <ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Asensio |first1=Pedro A. Guil |last2=Herzog |first2=Ivo |date=May 2004 |title=Left Cotorsion Rings |url=http://doi.wiley.com/10.1112/S0024609303002844 |journal=Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society |language=en |volume=36 |issue=3 |pages=303–309 |doi=10.1112/S0024609303002844 |issn=0024-6093|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
